newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA SAYS SUGAR BEET PLANTING ON SCHEDULE.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA SAYS SUGAR BEET PLANTING ON SCHEDULE.

text.p: Bulgaria's agricultural ministry said on Tuesday 5,000 hectares had been planted with sugar beet so far of a planned 8,000 hectares and it expected to meet its output target.

The ministry's plan for 1997 set the sugar beet area at 8,000 ha, up from last year's 6,000 but still far below 1995's beet area of 11,200 ha. It forecast sugar beet output of 120,000 tonnes, compared to 53,000 in 1996.
"I consider the figures realistic as the planting operations are proceeding as scheduled," said Valeri Iliev, head of the plant-growing department at the ministry.
Bulgaria's sugar output fell by 64 percent in 1996 due to bad weather in the spring. Farmers had difficulties obtaining funds due to the general economic crisis in the country.

But even with the expected higher output, Bulgaria, which used to meet nearly 50 percent of its sugar needs with local production, is expected to supply its sugar-processing plants with less than 10 percent of their needs. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2-91188
